response: ## Verdict: request changes — don't block **The evidence, verbatim from `crime_00037`:** ``` "byte size: 260,000 bytes (253.9 KB)" "severity ladder: low ≥ 200 KB · medium ≥ 500 KB · high ≥ 1000 KB" "format: png" ``` 253.9 KB puts it in the bottom band — 27% over the `low` threshold, half the `medium` threshold. `severity: low`, `agent_risk: 0.14`, `effort: quick`. Nothing here justifies gating a merge. But it's the **LCP element on the landing page**, which is the one place page weight converts directly into a Core Web Vitals number, and the fix is a two-minute re-encode. So: request changes, expect the fix in this PR rather than a follow-up ticket. ## What the finding doesn't tell you The evidence gives bytes and format but no dimensions — unlike `crime_00036`, which reports `32 × 32 px`. I read the PNG header directly: ``` src/assets/hero-banner.png: PNG image data, 1000 x 1000, 8-bit/color RGB, non-interlaced ``` Two things fall out of that: 1. **It's 8-bit RGB — no alpha channel.** PNG is a lossless codec being used on an asset that needs no transparency. That's the entire reason it's 254 KB; a lossy codec would carry the same pixels at a fraction of the size. This is a format mistake, not a size mistake. 2. **It's square.** A 1:1 asset labelled `hero-banner` will be cropped hard by any full-bleed hero band, meaning some of those 254 KB are pixels that never render at all. Also worth noting: `grep -rn "hero-banner" src/ docs/` returns nothing — nothing in the repo references the asset yet. If the PR adds the file without wiring it up, ask for the render site in the same PR; you can't size an image correctly without knowing its layout box. ## Recommended transformation **Target dimensions.** Size to the visible render area, not the source. For a standard full-bleed hero band (max container ~1440 CSS px, band height ~500–600 px), crop to a hero aspect — 16:9 or wider, not 1:1 — and ship a `srcset` rather than one file: | Variant | Serves | Byte budget (AVIF) | |---|---|---| | 768w × 432 | mobile 1x, small 2x | ≤ 35 KB | | 1280w × 720 | laptop 1x | ≤ 60 KB | | 1920w × 1080 | laptop 2x / desktop 1x | ≤ 110 KB | | 2560w × 1440 | desktop 2x (cap here) | ≤ 180 KB | Cap at 2560w. Serving beyond 2× DPR is spending bytes on pixels no display resolves. The variant most users actually download should land under ~150 KB — comfortably below today's single 254 KB file, at higher rendered fidelity. **Format: AVIF primary, WebP fallback.** Not either/or — `` with both: ```html ``` Why AVIF leads: - **Compression.** On photographic and gradient content AVIF typically lands 30–50% smaller than WebP at matched perceptual quality (AV1 intra-frame prediction vs WebP's VP8 keyframe encoder). - **Gradient handling, which matters specifically for heroes.** WebP lossy is locked to 8-bit 4:2:0 chroma. Hero images are usually large smooth gradients — skies, brand washes, blurred backgrounds — and 4:2:0 at hero scale is exactly where you see banding. AVIF supports 10-bit and 4:4:4, so it holds smooth tonal ramps at large render sizes without the stair-stepping. - **Support is no longer the objection.** Chrome 85+, Firefox 93+, Safari 16.4+ — ~95% globally, and the `` fallback covers the remainder losslessly. Why WebP stays as the fallback tier rather than being dropped: universal support (~97%), much faster encode in CI, and it degrades more gracefully than AVIF on hard edges and rendered text. **If this hero has baked-in text or sharp UI chrome, invert the recommendation** — lead with WebP at high quality, or AVIF at 4:4:4 with quality raised, because AVIF at aggressive settings smears fine high-contrast detail in a way that looks worse than WebP's artifacts. **Concretely, with `sharp`:** ```bash sharp -i hero-source.png -o hero-1920.avif resize 1920 1080 --fit cover -- avif --quality 55 sharp -i hero-source.png -o hero-1920.webp resize 1920 1080 --fit cover -- webp --quality 78 ``` If the site uses a framework image component (Next ``, Astro ``), skip the manual pipeline — set `formats: ['image/avif', 'image/webp']` and let it generate the ladder. Then delete `hero-banner.png` from the repo rather than leaving both. **Two things to ask for alongside the re-encode**, since they're free and this is the LCP element: explicit `width`/`height` (or `aspect-ratio`) to prevent layout shift, and `fetchpriority="high"` with no `loading="lazy"` — lazy-loading the LCP image is a common and self-inflicted LCP regression. ## One note on the rest of the PR If `src/assets/partner-logo.svg` is in the same diff, `crime_00032` is the finding worth more of your attention — `severity: high`, `confidence: 0.95`, two base64 rasters (`image/jpeg`, `image/png`) embedded inside a file whose MIME type promises vector. That one is a correctness problem (the asset lies about what it is and won't scale), not just a weight problem. Same review, higher priority.
